Hi everyone. I watched again the RTMA lite part 1. And i still a problem i can't resolve by myself up to now. In the lesson, a rule is stated -A LFL is a LFL if it broke a UFL and touched the next UFL. Vice versa for UFL. Rules are fine but understanding the inner logic behind it is better. My comprehension is that, in IT's mind, the logic is that before we go touch a zone of free order flow, to take salivan's concept, we'll let ourself some space to create mess and zones we can use on return. Once the mess is created, we go touch the zone and the mess making is over. It makes sense to me. Assuming that this is correct, there is still one problem: if the creation of a FL depends on the break of another FL, how do you determine that other FL is valid? At some point, there must be an other parameter, other than the "FL BREAK", which allows us to recognize and validate a FL. Otherwise this is just an equation that no one can resolve. I red probably every post made since the release of part 1 and I haven't seen any of them discussion that question. Like in IF's journal page 94-97, the UFL on the left are always considered as validated. Well i'm stuck at drawing these UFL on the left correctly so i'm stuck at finding good QMs/DMs. I made a big reading session of the QM homework section, it didn't help as the vast majority of post present the pattern, but not the FL they are a reaction to.

I'm turning round in circles for days now on that question, so if anyone has input on how to get forward with that, i'd be glad to read it!

The fact you are asking these questions shows you are heading down the right path. Think about this

A ufl needs to break a lfl and vice versa. What we have in between is the flag itself, when the flag body is in space it needs to complete the expansion by hitting the opposing ufl or lfl.

But every ufl or lfl has to start somewhere. It's like the chicken and the egg. Meaning as we go down in scale to mark them we only have limited data. This is a interesting thought. That's maybe because the FL article was written around the same time the dinosaurs went extinct. The FLs describe an area of imbalance, and initially was meant as a form of exercise for your eyes, kinda like the RBD/DBR thing but more

2920

advanced. People who took that exercise seriously on, did start to see what was the essence of it and why it was there. An FL is a marking on the right, of what was an imbalance on the left. It was always meant for to make people look at the left. IF's definition is the evolution of what it is and what we use it for.

HCDE, Looks like you are discovering FLs the new way it has been taught from IF. I like to stress again my definition of what I had posted before on someone else journal about FL. Here is it: FL = FTR = Kink. They are all the same. If you understand this and accept this, then things will be easier to comprehend going forward. Another way to try to understand the inner workings of a FL is try to understand the order flow as Harry have stated in terms of imbalances. We have FLs that are created which are not important/significant and ones that are significant. The significant one is the one what you should focus on. By significant I mean it needs to break a FL to its left. Think about order flow and imbalances rather than pattern and

I draw that diagram based on AUDUSD H1. I was wondering if the yellow box a kink? My answer to that is yes. As per IF definition and way of drawing in part 2, it seems perfectly legit, it's just a matter of scales like always. Thats a kink on H1 but that also a kink on H4. No problem with that. Then you can go lower timeframes and try to understand what happened and surely you'll find zones of interest. As i wrote on the chart, i see it as the entry into a small compression zone. On M1 it must look like a forest of lows, so lot of sells to absorb. Then they swap order into yellow price band: they bought sell stops, they now want to dump these buys. At the end they are short and shoot price down. So definitely have to look at it on H1 on return. I won't trade it though as there is a magnificent MPL just above. By the way there was a legit QM / DM from that MPL. I'll document it in my journal as it's one of the cleanest i've ever seen.

EDIT: The QM i talked about: readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/jou...hcde-s-journal#62721
